brief:
Mohammad Baraka, who served the European Union in Gaza for nearly two decades, described his situation as "devastating" after the organization terminated his employment without providing promised redundancy compensation, the Guardian reported. Unable to access the pay owed for his years of service, Baraka's family faces mounting financial hardship as their circumstances grow "increasingly desperate."

The case highlights the plight of Palestinian staff members caught between institutional employment structures and the humanitarian crisis engulfing Gaza, where access to funds and job opportunities remain severely constrained.
dek: Mohammad Baraka unable to access redundancy pay for almost 20 years’ service as family’s situation becomes ‘increasingly desperate’ A Palestinian man who worked for the EU in Gaza has told of a “devastating” struggle to survive after he was made redundant by…
title: Palestinian EU worker fights for redundancy pay after 20-year career ends
